prompts: A client loves the woodblock print attached, also in {WS}/print.jpg; it is in the public domain. They want a 3D wallpaper that copies it: its composition, its palette and its subjects, so anyone who knows the print recognizes it at a glance, rebuilt as our own low poly scene with some gentle motion. Deliver {WS}/scene/index.html, a single file with everything built in code: the print is the reference, not a texture. Record in {WS}/result.json what you took from it: boats (how many the print shows) and mountain (its name). It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
[goal] Low-poly 3D wallpaper of the print
[action] Inspected print.jpg via AGY vision; built scene/index.html (single file, Three.js from jsdelivr, Google Font); verified render via headless browser (canvas + WebGL active); wrote result.json
[result] The print is Hokusai's "The Great Wave off Kanagawa": 3 boats, Mount Fuji. Scene rebuilds asymmetrical wave (torus arc + foam claws) left/center, echo wave lower-left, three oared boats with rowers, snow-capped Fuji on the right horizon, Prussian-blue/cream/tan palette, cream sky, gentle motion (boat bob, claw shimmer, mist drift, camera sway). Assumptions: no texture used (geometry only); caption text as a nod to the title cartouche.
[next] Note: I could not visually confirm the render (this model has no image input; screenshot unreadable), so composition proportions are judgment, not verified. Browser tabs: one about:blank tab may remain open; I could not close it cleanly.
